points.statement: Aligning an LLM with environment dynamics is necessary and crucial for it to serve as a promising world model and enable more powerful embodied agents.
points.quote: In this paper, we show that aligning an LLM with environment dynamics is both necessary and crucial to make it a promising world model, which enables us to build more powerful embodied agents.

points.statement: A neurosymbolic world model combines a pretrained LLM with newly learned rules from interaction trajectories with the environment.
points.quote: In particular, we introduce a neurosymbolic world model that composites a pretrained LLM with a set of newly learned rules from the interaction trajectories with the environment.

points.statement: The world model combines LLM prior knowledge and reasoning with hard constraints and rigorous guarantees enforced by rules.
points.quote: This specific form of world model combines the strengths of both in modeling the environment dynamics, i.e., (1) the rich prior knowledge, probabilistic, and deductive reasoning capability of LLMs (Hu & Shu 2023); and (2) the hard constraints and rigorous guarantees enforced by rules (Li et al. 2024a).

points.statement: In the method, only a few complementary rules suffice to align a pretrained LLM to specific environment dynamics.
points.quote: While creating a rule-only world model for a complex environment is challenging due to the massive amount of rules and uncertainty (Xiao et al. 2021), in our method, only a few complementary rules suffice to align a pretrained LLM to specific environment dynamics.

points.statement: Including these rules in the LLM prompt achieves alignment without tedious training or inference.
points.quote: This is achieved by simply including these rules in the LLM’s prompt without tedious training or inference.

points.statement: A neurosymbolic approach learns rules gradient-free through LLMs by inducing, updating, and pruning rules from comparisons of explored trajectories and world model predictions.
points.quote: To this end, we propose a neurosymbolic approach to learn these rules gradient-free through LLMs, by inducing, updating, and pruning rules based on comparisons of agent-explored trajectories and world model predictions.

points.statement: With rich prior knowledge in LLMs, only a few additional rules suffice to align LLM predictions with specified environment dynamics.
points.quote: Given the rich prior knowledge of LLMs, only a few additional rules suffice to align LLM predictions with the specified environment dynamics.

points.statement: The resulting world model consists of the LLM and the learned rules.
points.quote: The resulting world model is composed of the LLM and the learned rules.

points.statement: An LLM analyzes comparison results to extract new rules or modify existing ones, improving consistency between predicted and real trajectories.
points.quote: The comparison results are then analyzed by an LLM, which extracts new rules or modifies existing ones to improve the consistency between the predicted and real trajectories.

points.statement: At each iteration end, rules are pruned by selecting a subset with maximal coverage of transitions the LLM failed to predict.
points.quote: To keep the rule set minimal necessarily, at the end of each iteration, we prune the rules by solving a maximum coverage problem, which aims to select a subset of rules with the maximal coverage of the transitions failed being predicted by the LLM in the world model (without applying any rules).

points.statement: The selected rules are complementary to the LLM predictions.
points.quote: Hence, the selected rules are complementary to the LLM predictions.

points.statement: The rule learning procedure repeats for multiple iterations until the LLM plus rules performs as an accurate world model.
points.quote: The above rule learning procedure repeats for multiple iterations until the LLM+rules performs as an accurate world model.
